name: Inven Capital
decision_note: Prague-based, ČEZ-backed corporate VC (self-managed SICAV, EUR 500m) investing in later-stage climate tech; co-led Wint's USD 36m Series D (Sept 2026) and joined Andercore's USD 40m Series B (Feb 2026).

evidence.quote: As a venture capital fund we invest EUR 500m from institutional investors and global corporates in the most innovative startups in the world.
Inven Capital is a EUR 500m European VC fund focused on later-stage climate tech investments in Europe & Israel, backed by CEZ Group and European Investment Bank (EIB).
It primarily focuses on later-stage growth investment opportunities with a sound business model proven by realized revenues and long-term growth potential.
Wint, the leading provider of water management solutions for the built environment, today announced it has raised $36 million in Series D funding co-led by LIP Ventures and Inven Capital.
Participating investors include long-term partners Atomico and Project A, with Inven Capital joining this round, alongside institutional financing from Commerzbank and KfW.
With a total fund size of more than €500 million, Inven has bolstered its position as a strong and stable partner for innovative startups and co-investors, including major global players.
Inven co-leads $40M Series B in Andercore
Inven’s portfolio company Woltair raises €16.3m to help Europeans heat and power their homes

analyst_notes: Corporate VC of the ČEZ Group (flag corporate); the 2024 annual report states the SICAV is a self-managed investment fund (samosprávný investiční fond) controlled by ČEZ, so the SICAV is listed as manager and its four sub-funds (Podfond A-D, IČO from ARES) as fund vehicles. Capital EUR 500m: stated on the homepage (undated), in the Wint release boilerplate (2026-09-09, used as as_of) and in Inven's own Vytal release (2 July 2026, '€500 million under management'); the EIB release of 2023-02-08 (EIB committed a further EUR 50m for the 2022-2027 investment period) gives 'total fund size of more than €500 million' - recorded as the fund commitment event. CVCA profile (2020, self-reported) split it as 250m (sub-funds A+B) + 250m (C+D). Stage: 'later-stage growth' mapped to series_b/growth (observed rounds Series B-D). Ticket EUR 2-30m stated on the homepage, same as CVCA. Geography 'Europe and Israel' (IL as ISO code). Investments: Wint USD 36m Series D co-led with LIP Ventures (Wint is the Israeli water-intelligence company; dateline New York; country IL); Andercore USD 40m Series B 'in equity and debt' (round amount includes debt), Inven's homepage says Inven co-led it while Andercore's release says Inven 'joining this round'. Inven also published a 2 July 2026 Vytal growth-capital release (PDF on its site) that quotes an Inven investment director but does not name the investors, so it is not used as investment evidence. The annual-report PDF appears to have an OCR text layer, so only a short quote is used from it. [revision 2026-10-25 re-audit: scope rule: the cited in-window deals are Israeli and German, so a Czech portfolio company is now evidenced - Woltair (Prague heat-pump/solar installer, woltair.cz) named as 'Inven's portfolio company' on Inven's homepage news list (e13, undated, links a Sifted article on 'Czech Woltair'); office Prague. Type re-checked under the dominant-activity rule: Inven writes EUR 2-30m minority tickets in Series B-D rounds of VC-backed climate-tech startups alongside VCs (Wint, Andercore) and describes itself as a venture capital fund - growth-stage VC, not late-stage/pre-IPO/secondaries, so vc (corporate, ČEZ) is kept. Capital (EUR 500m committed/under management, aum), activity (Wint 2026-09-09) and ticket unchanged.]
